diagnosed: Visual QA agent fails nearly every day (not quota — usage green, 8% weekly). Always a turn-budget overrun: most runs 'reported a successful result after 41/42 turns, exceeding the configured maximum of 40' (work done + committed, but run marked failure), some hit the hard 'Reached maximum number of turns (40)' before committing (e.g. 2026-10-27, no visual-qa commit). Root cause: the task (3 screenshots + 3 image reads + DESIGN.md + write + git push-with-rebase) legitimately lands at 41-42 turns, just over the 40 budget; the prompt had the agent run the three screenshots and read the three images as separate steps, spending ~4 easily-batched turns.
fixed: scripts/agents/visual-qa.md: chain the three screenshot.js calls into one Bash call and read all three screenshots in one step; added a note to keep tool calls lean under the bounded turn budget (~4 turns reclaimed, moving a normal run back under 40).
notes: npm test green: 1546 passed / 88 files (incl. workflows + agent-prompts coherence tests).
Turn reduction is reasoned, not run-verified — the full Sonnet agent run can't be executed here.

The robust fix is a one-line bump of --max-turns 40 -> 60 in .github/workflows/visual-qa-agent.yml (peers editorial/coverage-critic already at 60), but that is a protected automation path the protect-automation CI hook forbids an unattended agent from authoring — a human must make that edit. Called out in the PR body as a request to the owner.

No other real breakage found: validate-events.js clean (warnings only), publish-freshness fresh (lag 0h), no open self-repair PRs. Research-agent failures in the window line up with the quota governor's domain, not self-repair's.
